title: Hubble captures glittering crowded hub of our Milky Way
caption: Stars in the crowded central bulge of the Milky Way, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Stars · constellation Sagittarius · about 25000 light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA, and T. Brown (STScI), W. Clarkson (University of Michigan-Dearborn), and A. Calamida and K. Sahu (STScI)

recognition.text: Published in the ESA/Hubble image archive. No published rating.

story: A crowd of stars fills this Hubble view of the heart of our galaxy. Ageing red giants mingle with their more plentiful younger relatives, smaller, white, Sun-like stars, in the Milky Way's ancient central hub, known as the bulge. Most of the bright blue stars are probably recently formed stars in the foreground, in the galaxy's disc.

Working through nine years of archived Hubble images, astronomers tracked 10 000 of these Sun-like stars, looking for clues to how our galaxy evolved. They found the bulge is a busy place, where stars of different ages move at different speeds, like travelers rushing through an airport.

How a star moves depends on its chemistry. Stars with more elements beyond hydrogen and helium move in a more orderly way, yet they circle the galactic center faster than older stars that lack such elements.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.20 x 1.86 arcminutes) and distance (25000 light years), the frame spans roughly 16 × 14 light-years. Its light set out about 25,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This composite combines visible and near-infrared exposures from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3. The source does not publish which color was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: Near-infrared light is invisible to the eye, so part of this picture records light we could never see directly.

explore: The data were gathered for the Galactic Bulge Treasury Program and for the Sagittarius Window Eclipsing Extrasolar Planet Search, two separate Hubble surveys. Our galaxy's center lies roughly 26 000 light-years from Earth.
alt: A dense field of stars, with red giants, many white Sun-like stars and some bright blue stars.
